area: Mod-addable UI surfaces in Big Ambitions (phone apps, BizMan tabs, native windows, ModOptions, notifications, phone messages)
findings:
## 1. New smartphone app or new BizMan tab — HARD-CODED, no API, not moddable natively

`AppName` (decomp/BigAmbitions/AppName.cs) is a plain 8-value `enum`: Persona, Contacts, MyEmployees, BizMan, EconoView, VoogleMaps, MarketInsider, Rivals. Apps are built from a serialized ScriptableObject:
- `SmartphoneApps : ScriptableObject { SmartphoneApp[] appList; }`, `SmartphoneApp { AppName appName; bool showInFullMenu; Sprite icon; }` — both `[SerializeField]` on `SmartphoneUI` / `FullMenu`.
- `SmartphoneUI.Awake()` and `FullMenu.Start()` iterate `apps.appList` to spawn app buttons into `appButtons` / `_appButtons` dictionaries keyed by `AppName`.
- `FullMenu.SelectApp(AppName)` shows a view by locating the `appsContainer` child transform whose `name == appName.ToStringFast()`. Every app view is a pre-authored scene GameObject.
- `SmartphoneUI.OpenApp(string)` does `Enum.TryParse<AppName>`; `FullMenu.ShowApp(string)` does `Enum.Parse<AppName>` — a string not in enum metadata fails/throws.

There is NO `RegisterApp`/`AddApp`/`AddTab`/`RegisterTab`/`RegisterWindow` anywhere in `BigAmbitions.ModAPI.decompiled.cs` or in `ModsInternal/`.

`ModsInternal/ModEnumDefinitions.cs` DOES let a mod add enum values: it reads `<modRoot>/enums.txt` (lines like `Namespace.EnumType.NEW_VALUE`), resolves the type with `Type.GetType`, and computes an int via `BAModAPI.ModEnumHash.GetSafeHash` (SHA256-derived, forced above 2000 to avoid collisions with real values). BUT this only fills a private side-dictionary `DefinedEnumValueNames` used for conflict detection / data-driven lookups. It does NOT teach `Enum.GetName` / `Enum.Parse` / the Roslyn-generated `ToStringFast()` about the value, and creates no GameObject / icon / view / handler. So enums.txt is usable for data enums (item categories, business types the game looks up by hash), NOT for wiring a working phone app or tab.

BizMan tabs (decomp/BigAmbitions/UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan/BizMan.cs): 16 `const string` tab ids. `BizManBusiness.SetUpTabs()` builds a private `List<string> _tabs` via hard-coded `.Add("Schedule")` / `.Add("HRManagers")` etc. per `businessTypeName`. `BizManBusiness.SetTab(name)` does `menu.Find(name)` + `containers.Find(name)` on serialized child transforms and a hard-coded `switch(tabName)` for per-tab init. Adding a tab requires: a bundled menu-button prefab + container prefab, reflection into `_tabs`, and Harmony patches on `SetUpTabs`/`SetTab`. Not supported natively; fragile even with Harmony.

## 2. Native-styled window/panel at runtime — NO dedicated API; achievable via asset bundles + game DraggableWindows

There is NO `ModWindow` / `IModWindow` / `NativeWindow` / `BaseWindow` / `WindowController` type in `BigAmbitions.ModAPI` or `ModsInternal`. The SDK docs' "native game-styled windows" corresponds to no shipped type — treat it as not available.

What actually exists for runtime UI:
- `BAModAPI.Services.AssetService` (full asset-bundle pipeline). `IModBigAmbitions.RelativeAssetBundlePaths` declares bundle files; `AssetService.RegisterBundle / GetBundle / GetAllAssetNames / FindAssetInAnyBundleByFileName<T> / Spawn(...) / SpawnAsync(...)` load prefabs and `UnityEngine.Object.Instantiate` them. `AssetService.RemapShaders(GameObject, fallbackShaderName=null)` re-points prefab materials onto the game's own shaders (built from `Resources.FindObjectsOfTypeAll<Shader>()`), so a bundled UI prefab renders correctly against the game build. A mod ships a Unity-authored Canvas/panel prefab, loads it, and parents it under a game UI transform reached via `InstanceBehavior<UIs>.Instance...`.
- `UI.DraggableWindows.DraggableWindows` (game class, `public`, singleton via `InstanceBehavior<DraggableWindows>.Instance`, also `InstanceBehavior<UIs>.Instance.draggableWindows`). Public `RegisterDraggableWindow(DraggableWindows.Data { string id; RectTransform element; DraggableWindowHandle handle; Vector3 defaultPosition; })` gives drag behaviour + automatic position persistence (via `PlayerSettingsHelper`, saved on `GlobalEvents.onSaveGame`). The mod must supply the `RectTransform` and a `DraggableWindowHandle` component (game MonoBehaviour: `IPointerDownHandler`/`IPointerUpHandler`, exposes `isDragging`, `offset`, `OnDragEnded`).
- `UI.CollapsibleWindow` — the collapsible-window widget used by the smartphone (game class; name shows as `n` in this decomp due to obfuscation of the file's primary type).

Net: a mod CAN put a custom, draggable, shader-correct panel on screen, but it authors the visuals itself (bundle prefab, hand-styled to match, or cloned at runtime from a game window prefab) — there is no "give me a native window" call.

## 3. ModOptions — every control type, and it DOES show in-game

`BigAmbitions.Mods.ModOptions` (fluent builder, in `BigAmbitions.ModAPI.dll`):
- `AddHeader(string label)` -> `HeaderOption`
- `AddSplitter()` -> `SplitterOption`
- `AddButton(string label, Action onClick=null)` -> `ButtonOption`
- `AddToggle(string id, string label, bool defaultValue, Action<bool> onValueChanged=null)` -> `ToggleOption` (persisted)
- `AddSlider(string id, string label, int min, int max, int defaultValue, Action<int> onValueChanged=null, string valueLabelKey=null)` -> `SliderOption` (persisted; INT only — no float slider)
- `AddDropdown(string id, string label, string[] choiceKeys, int defaultIndex=0, Action<int> onValueChanged=null)` -> `DropdownOption` (persisted)
- `AddCustom(ModOption option)` — escape hatch. Subclass `ModOption`, override `SpawnUi(Transform parent, string modId)`. `ModOptionsViewController.SpawnOption` calls `option.SpawnUi(contentRoot, modId)` whenever `ResolvePrefab` returns null (any type other than the 6 built-ins), handing you the content-root `Transform` to instantiate arbitrary UGUI into.
There is NO plain text/label control except `AddHeader`, NO image control, NO text-input field.

Registration: `OptionsService.Register(string modId, ModOptions)`, `OptionsService.RemoveModOptions(modId)`, `OptionsService.ResetAllToDefaults()`; events `OptionsService.OnChanged`, `OptionsService.OnReset`; `OptionsService.RegisteredEntries` (IReadOnlyDictionary). Persisted controls (`IPersistableOption`: Toggle/Slider/Dropdown) need a non-empty, unique `id` or the value is not saved (logs an error). Persistence sink is `PlayerPrefs` key `"m:{modId}:{optionId}"` (see `ModOptionsViewController.ClearOptionPrefs` and `ModsInternal/ModOptionPrefs.cs`).

WHERE it renders — BOTH main menu and in-game:
- `Scenes.MainMenu.Options` is a single shared MonoBehaviour (`InstanceBehavior<UIs>.Instance.options`) used by the main menu AND the in-game pause menu. It has `[Header("Mods")] GameObject modsTabButton`. `Options.RefreshModsTabButton()` sets `modsTabButton.SetActive(OptionsService.RegisteredEntries.Count > 0)` and subscribes to `OptionsService.OnChanged` — the "Mods" category button only appears once a mod has registered options.
- `ModsInternal/ModOptionsViewController.cs` (MonoBehaviour) is the renderer inside that Mods tab. It is referenced NOWHERE in code — wired purely via Unity scene/prefab serialization (serialized fields: `contentRoot` + one prefab per built-in control). `OnEnable` subscribes to `OptionsService.OnChanged`/`OnReset` and calls `Rebuild()`, which destroys `contentRoot` children and re-spawns every option of every registered mod. `SpawnOption` -> `ResolvePrefab` (built-in) via `IModOptionsControl.Initialize(option)` on the instantiated prefab, else `option.SpawnUi(...)`.
- In-game path: `UI.MiniMenu.MiniMenu.OpenOptions()` -> `InstanceBehavior<UIs>.Instance.options.SetActive(true); Options.IsVisible = true;` and `CloseOptions()` mirrors it. Same object, so the Mods options panel is reachable from the pause menu (Esc -> Options -> Mods) as well as the main-menu Options screen.

So ModOptions is a settings list (not a free-form dashboard) that IS available during play, but it lives in the settings screen, not "the office".

## 4. Notifications.Show and Contact/TextMessage — exact working calls

(a) Toast — `UI.Notification.Notifications` (static):
```
Notifications.Show(
    NotificationType.Success,                 // enum order: Success, Warning, Error, Info
    "sm:notif_restock_done",                  // headerKey -> key.Localize(data)
    new Dictionary<string,string>{{"store",reg.BusinessName},{"amount","12"}},
    4f,                                        // secondsToShow
    "sm-restock-"+reg.Address,                // duplicateIdentifier (null => allow dupes)
    () => { /* onClick */ },                   // onClickAction (optional)
    true,                                      // notificationSound
    true);                                     // trackOnSaveGame -> enqueued into SaveGameManager.Current.notifications (history)
```
`Notifications.onShow` is bound by `NotificationsUI` in the city scene; if invoked in the main menu / too early it logs "No Notifications found" and no-ops — call only after city load. `headerKey` and the placeholder substitution go through `key.Localize(notificationData)` in `NotificationsUI.ShowNotification`. The game only ever passes real localization keys here; a mod should register its keys via a `Locales/` folder (see below). Convenience: `Notifications.ShowError(headerKey, duplicateIdentifier=null, trackOnSaveGame=true)`.

(b) Phone message from a named contact — `Entities.Contact` + `Entities.TextMessage`:
```
using Entities; using UI.Smartphone.Apps.Contacts;
Contact c = Contact.GetContact(
    "Store Manager",                       // id (== display name); dedup key is (id, description)
    ContactCategoryName.Employees,
    "employee_contact_description",         // description; this exact string => IsEmployeeContact => employee icon
    null,                                  // Address (optional)
    false);                               // hasWelcomeMessages
c.SendMessage(
    new TextMessage("sm:msg_daily_digest",
        new Dictionary<string,string>{{"store",reg.BusinessName},{"sold","34"}},
        read:false, isNewInteraction:true),
    notify:true,
    sendNotificationInstantly:false);      // false => batched via ContactsHelper (coalesced, max 5); true => immediate
```
`ContactCategoryName` (decomp/BigAmbitions/UI.Smartphone.Apps.Contacts/ContactCategoryName.cs) = General, Business, Finance, FurnitureAndEquipment, ImportsAndGoods, Employees, Rivals. The contact is stored in `SaveGameManager.Current.Contacts` and serialized into the save; use `Contact.EnsurePermanentContact(id, category, description)` on load to keep a single instance. `SendMessage` bumps the Contacts app badge (`SmartphoneUI.UpdateBadgeCount(AppName.Contacts)`), appends live if the Contacts app is open, else raises a "new message" notification via `ContactsHelper`. `messagesQueue` is FIFO capped at 20 (`Contact.MaxMessages`).

Contact icon: `Contact.GetPredefinedIconSprite()` matches `sprite.name` against `InstanceBehavior<GlobalReferences>.Instance.contactIcons` using the contact `id` (or literal `"employee"` when `IsEmployeeContact`). An unknown id with a non-employee description just yields a null icon (blank, no crash). There is NO ModAPI path to register a custom contact icon; set `description = "employee_contact_description"` to borrow the generic employee icon. Debug helper: `Contact.Command_ReceiveMessage(ContactCategoryName, string messageKey)` (`[ConsoleMethod("ReceiveMessage", ...)]`).

Mod localization: `ModsInternal/ModDiscoveryRegistry.SyncDiscoveredLocalizationPaths()` scans each mod folder for a `Locales/` subdirectory and calls `LocalizorManager.SyncExternalLocalizationPaths({ modId : <modRoot>/Locales })`; `ModsInternal/ModLifecycleLoader` then calls `LocalizorManager.LoadLocalizationTables(reloadIndex:false)`. So shipping `<modRoot>/Locales/` (game Localizor table format) is the supported way to make custom `headerKey` / `messageKey` values resolve. (The `Localizor` assembly itself is not in this decomp, so the exact table file format is unconfirmed.)

## 5. Ranked answer: where can a mod give the player a place to hire + configure a manager

1. NEW PHONE APP — NOT POSSIBLE natively (no registry; `AppName` enum, app buttons, and app views are all serialized/hard-wired; `Enum.Parse` round-trips on names). Only Harmony + bundled prefabs could fake it, patching `SmartphoneUI`/`FullMenu`; fragile across updates. Not recommended.
2. NATIVE WINDOW/PANEL — PARTIALLY POSSIBLE. No "spawn game window" API, but ship a Unity UI prefab in an asset bundle (`RelativeAssetBundlePaths` + `AssetService.Spawn`), parent it under a game canvas, run `AssetService.RemapShaders`, and optionally `DraggableWindows.Instance.RegisterDraggableWindow(...)` for drag + saved position. The mod authors all visuals/interactions. This is the best route to a real hire/configure screen; cost is building it in Unity and shipping a bundle. Feasible.
3. MODOPTIONS PANEL — FULLY POSSIBLE, least effort, visible in-game (pause menu -> Options -> Mods tab, appears once `OptionsService.Register` is called). Header/Button/Toggle/int-Slider/Dropdown + `AddCustom.SpawnUi(parent)` for arbitrary UGUI. Good for: choose manager skill, "Hire" button, per-store budget slider, staffing-level dropdown, feature toggles. Limits: no text input, int-only sliders, flat list not a dashboard, buried in settings (not "the office"). Pragmatic default; the existing mod already uses this.
4. DEBUG CONSOLE — POSSIBLE, always works, not player-facing. `IngameDebugConsole.CommandHelper.AddCommand[/<T1..T5>](string command, string description, Delegate/Action/Func method)` + `RemoveCommand`, or `[ConsoleMethod(cmd, desc, paramNames)]` on a static method (ExternalPlugins.dll). The existing mod already registers `StoreManager.Hire` etc. this way. Dev/power-user only.

Bottom line vs the user's vision: "hire the Store Manager THROUGH THE OFFICE/HQ exactly like the HR/Pricing/Logistics Manager" is NOT reachable without Harmony — those live in `Buildings.Office.Headquarters` + the hard-wired `HRManagers`/`PricingManagers`/`LogisticsManagers` BizMan tabs, and the game resolves them by fixed enum/string names with no mod hook. Visible feedback (point 1 of the design) IS fully reachable: `Notifications.Show` toasts + `Contact`/`TextMessage` phone messages + optionally a bundled draggable panel. The "hire + configure" surface must be a ModOptions "Mods" tab (available now, in-game) or a bundled asset-bundle panel opened from a hotkey / console / notification-click — not the office screen. Injecting a real BizMan "Store Managers" tab is only conceivable with a bundled Harmony dependency (another local mod already bundles Harmony this way) and is a large, brittle effort.

modFeasibility:
NATIVE (no Harmony, ModAPI only):
- Toasts: YES — UI.Notification.Notifications.Show, after city load. Confirmed by existing mod.
- Phone messages from a named contact: YES — Entities.Contact.GetContact/EnsurePermanentContact + Contact.SendMessage(new TextMessage(...)). Persists in the save. Custom contact icon: NO (falls back to blank or the employee icon).
- Custom text keys for notifications/messages: YES — ship <modRoot>/Locales/ (game Localizor table format; exact file format unverified — the Localizor assembly is not in the decomp).
- ModOptions settings list: YES, and it shows in-game (pause menu -> Options -> Mods, appears after OptionsService.Register). Controls: Header, Splitter, Button, Toggle, int Slider, Dropdown, plus AddCustom+SpawnUi(parent) for arbitrary UGUI in the options content root. No text input, no float slider, no data grid.
- Custom on-screen panel/window: YES via asset bundle — declare RelativeAssetBundlePaths, AssetService.Spawn the prefab, AssetService.RemapShaders, parent under a game canvas (InstanceBehavior<UIs>.Instance...). Optionally DraggableWindows.Instance.RegisterDraggableWindow for drag + saved position. Mod authors all visuals and interactions; requires a Unity project to build the bundle.
- Debug console commands: YES — IngameDebugConsole.CommandHelper.AddCommand / [ConsoleMethod]. Not player-facing.

NEEDS HARMONY (mod can bundle Harmony as a flat Dependencies/ DLL, as another local mod already does):
- New BizMan tab (e.g. 'Store Managers' beside HRManagers): patch BizManBusiness.SetUpTabs (inject into private _tabs) + SetTab (init/activate the mod container) + supply bundled menu-button and container prefabs. Large, brittle, breaks on game UI updates.
- New smartphone app: patch SmartphoneUI.Awake / FullMenu.Start / FullMenu.SelectApp + bundled app-view prefab + intercept Enum.Parse<AppName> string paths. Even more invasive.
- Hooking into the actual Office/Headquarters manager-hire screen (HrManagerPlan-style): no seam found; would require patching Buildings.Office.Headquarters UI classes. Effectively a rewrite of that screen.

INFEASIBLE / NOT FOUND:
- Any 'RegisterApp' / 'AddTab' / 'RegisterWindow' / 'ModWindow' / native game-window factory API. Does not exist in BigAmbitions.ModAPI or ModsInternal.
- Registering a custom ContactPreset or contact icon through the ModAPI.

RECOMMENDATION for the 7-point design: deliver visible feedback with Notifications + Contact/TextMessage (native, confirmed). Put the hire/configure surface in either (a) a ModOptions 'Mods' tab (works today, in-game, lowest effort) or (b) a bundled asset-bundle panel opened via hotkey/console/notification-click (more work, closer to the 'real UI' feel). Accept that 'hire through the Office exactly like the HR Manager' and 'manager appears in My Employees via the same flow' are not achievable through mod-facing APIs — at best approximated with Harmony patches against hard-coded UI.
openQuestions: Exact file format the game's Localizor expects for a mod's <modRoot>/Locales/ folder (CSV? per-language columns? key naming rules?) — the Localizor assembly is not in the decomp; needs an in-game test or a look at Big Ambitions_Data/Managed/Localizor*.dll / an existing localized mod.

Whether NotificationsUI's key.Localize() returns the raw string as a fallback when a key is missing (so raw English text 'just works') or renders an empty/placeholder string — determines if a Locales/ table is mandatory for mod notifications/messages.

Whether AssetService can load a UI prefab whose canvas/material references resolve correctly after RemapShaders in practice for TextMeshPro + game UI shaders, or if additional font/material rebinding is needed (only testable in-game).

Whether cloning an existing game window/panel prefab at runtime (via Resources.FindObjectsOfTypeAll or AssetService.FindAssetInAnyBundleByFileName) is viable for a 'native look' without shipping custom art — not verified.

Exact members of DraggableWindowHandle (the decomp file was not opened) — confirm the handle component can be added to a mod-built RectTransform and that OnDragEnded/isDragging/offset are the full surface RegisterDraggableWindow relies on.

Confirm the in-game pause-menu Options screen actually instantiates/enables the ModOptionsViewController subtree at runtime (it is scene-serialized and not code-referenced) — i.e. that the 'Mods' tab content renders in-game and not only in the main menu.
Whether a mod adding a value to AppName via enums.txt causes exceptions anywhere the game calls Enum.Parse<AppName> / ToStringFast on iteration (could destabilize the phone UI) — needs a test.
